group.passage:
The Rashomon Effect is a term used to explain how a single event can be described in contradictory ways. The term was coined after legendary filmmaker Akira Kurosawa first applied this storytelling technique in Rashomon (1950). [[1]] As different versions of events unfold, the audience is also able to understand the characters in many dimensions. There have been countless films, television shows, literature, court cases, and journalism influenced by the Rashomon Effect since the film was released.
The story centers around a sexual assault on a bride and the murder of her samurai husband, recalled by four witnesses in a trial with contrasting descriptions. [[2]] Truth then becomes a puzzle of perspectives. This mirrors the fake news we see on social media today.
On social media, people’s beliefs and biases shape what they share and how they see what others post. Their takes and versions blend with genuine news, plus social media’s reach, creating a maze of truths, half-truths, and pure lies. As a result, the line between fact and fiction blurs, and the real story gets lost in the noise. This makes fake news look like real news, especially when it’s designed to play on our emotions and beliefs. [[3]] However, since news floods in from numerous online sources in today’s world, it’s impossible to know what’s been checked for accuracy.
Despite this, the truth does exist. It is just buried under layers of misinformation that cloud its clarity. [[4]] Just like in Rashomon, Kurosawa allows his audience to question the motives of each individual and explores the fragile nature of human memory. We should always question what we see and hear in order to seek out the truth that lies beyond our screens.

options_bank.A: All seem true but conflict with one another.
options_bank.B: Journalists once acted as the gatekeepers of news, ensuring facts were verified.
options_bank.C: This narrative style allows the audience to see a single story through multiple lenses.
options_bank.D: To uncover this hidden truth, we must engage in critical thinking and maintain a healthy level of doubt.
